samples.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
samples.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
samples.relation: Abigail Myers runs Stoic doctrine against Katniss's biography: Zeno's thesis that only moral goodness is good (with Plutarch Heavensbee's renunciation of Capitol privilege as indifference to wealth and status), Seneca's 'On the Shortness of Life' against deferring living, Epictetus's dichotomy of control including the uncomfortable advice to kiss wife and child as mortals, and Marcus Aurelius's practical Meditations as the gentler 'Stoic for beginners' who would be president of Panem. Katniss comes out Stoic in her frugality, her mortality-shadowed appreciation of small joys, and her firm moral code, but decidedly un-Stoic in her fierce attachments to Rue, Peeta, and Prim. Yet her final choice of Peeta over Gale is itself Stoic, Myers argues: she forgives what Peeta's hijacking made him do since it was never in his control, refuses a noble friendship that would endorse Gale and Coin's slaughter of innocents, and chooses in accordance with nature and reason so as to survive as herself with her values intact.

samples.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
samples.title: Sometimes We Can Let Go
samples.relation: Sets the intuition that angry blame is how we hold people responsible (Strawson; Katara's useful fury at Pakku's sexism, Iroh's 'whatever you do to that spirit, I will unleash on you tenfold') against the Senecan and Buddhist verdict that anger is greedy for revenge, and reads ATLA as modeling ways to hold people responsible without toxic anger. In 'The Southern Raiders' Katara neither forgives Yon Rha nor kills him, showing that blame can be set down when expressing it is pointless, while she forgives Zuko in Lucy Allais's 'wiping the slate clean' sense because his past betrayal no longer speaks to his present character. Iroh's handling of the mugger in Ba Sing Se ('I was never angry; I was afraid that you had lost your way') models responding to the suffering behind wrongdoing with compassion instead of blame, and Zuko's self-anger is diagnosed as hypocritical self-blame whose antidote is self-compassion: acknowledging how he himself was hurt is what finally lets him take ownership of his wrongs.

samples.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
samples.title: 15. Bias Is Rational!
samples.relation: Percival, whose Myth of the Closed Mind Adams cites, rebuts the Moist Robot Hypothesis that visual, emotional, repetitive anchors make us ninety-percent irrational. Against Kahneman's fast-and-dumb System 1 he sets Gigerenzer's ecological rationality (the gaze-angle heuristic that catches fly balls, the recognition heuristic that lets ignorant German students beat Americans on Detroit versus Milwaukee), then goes further with Popper's critical rationalism: babies as little scientists conjecturing and refuting, experience always theory-laden (the duck-rabbit), and Newton's boy on the seashore facing an infinite but navigable ocean of error elimination. The Stoic insight that all emotion is thoughtful and all thought emotional (the falling-tiles misperception that flips anger to relief) shows feelings track beliefs, so a free battle of the biases, not fact-free affirmation in the lineage of Le Bon and Pavlovian conditioning, is how rationality actually works.

samples.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
samples.title: A Nietzschean Conclusion
samples.relation: Slowik argues the Pythons have a positive existentialist message: Kafka's bureaucratic insanity, where ordinary people beat helplessly against irrational rules, recurs in the 'Cheese Shop' and 'Dead Parrot' sketches, and Camus's Sisyphus lives on in the monotonous lives of Palin's city stockbroker and the accountant who dreams of lion taming — repetition without Sisyphus's defiance. The core claim is that Python endorses individual-centered existentialism: Brian's 'You've got to think for yourselves. You're all individuals!' is the troupe's rare direct statement of Sartre's 'existence precedes essence', confirmed by Cleese's and Palin's interviews about resisting those who tell you how to behave, a theme the chapter extends through Nietzsche's critique of moral tradition and organized Christianity. Sartrean bad faith explains Python's stereotyped characters — the aggressive policeman, the pepperpots, and Mr. Praline insisting 'I am not a loony!' while demanding a fish license for his halibut — while Arthur Pewtey's meek 'Right. Right.' and Ron Obvious's physical limits raise nature/nurture objections to Sartrean freedom. The 'Nietzschean Conclusion' is that Monty Python itself exemplifies will to power as 'giving style' to one's character, constantly overcoming its own formulas rather than repeating what succeeded.

samples.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
samples.title: A Political Philosophy of Vampires
samples.relation: Phillip Cole starts from Rousseau's remark that the eighteenth-century vampire epidemics had complete legal proof, and argues the panics — like the witch craze Trevor-Roper ties to the Reformation's power struggles — reveal how political authorities constitute borders and power by cultivating fear of imaginary enemies. Freud's uncanny (fear not of death but of the returning dead) and Kristeva's abject (the corpse as the ultimate waste) explain why the Undead horrify and fascinate — Scratchy's ever-watching eyes in Itchy and Scratchy, the drowning corpse in Thérèse Raquin, Six Feet Under's serener dead and its wryly absurdist tone — while the vampire also plays the romantic monster of Coppola's Dracula and Interview with the Vampire. Politically the vampire is the demonized outsider — Stoker's unassimilated Jewish immigrant, today's asylum seeker or terrorist — and Buffy blurs the boundary by making demons neighbors and Angel and Spike heroes, while the truly shocking killings (Faith's accidental shooting of a human ally, Warren's gunning down of Tara) are human, all too human. The chapter concludes that we should stop mistaking fear-made borders for moral ones and the constructed outsider for a mortal enemy.

samples.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
samples.title: A Political Philosophy of Vampires
samples.relation: Phillip Cole takes Rousseau's remark that the eighteenth-century vampire epidemics had complete legal proof - the Arnold Paole exhumations - and argues Rousseau's real point was political: authorities manufacture imaginary monsters, as in the witch craze, to exploit fear and hold power over their own populations. Freud's account of the uncanny explains why the horror is not death itself but the returning dead (the watching eyes of Scratchy in Itchy and Scratchy, versus the serene corpses of Six Feet Under, whose absurdity the show meets with wry amusement), and Julia Kristeva's abjection explains the corpse as the ultimate boundary-breaker. The vampire then resurfaces as the demonized outsider - Stoker's Dracula coded as the unassimilated Jewish immigrant, today's terrorist - exposing political borders as arbitrary fabrications. Buffy completes the collapse of the us/them binary: Angel and Spike join the slayer, and the most shocking killings (Faith's accidental human kill, Warren's stray bullet hitting Tara) are all too human, so the real subject of border policing is the community's own members.

samples.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
samples.title: How to Misunderstand Politics Completely
samples.relation: Melançon argues Radiohead's real politics lie not in the overt content of Hail to the Thief but in a Camusian movement from absurdity to revolt: 'Exit Music'''s violent shift from Romeo's tender 'you' to the distorted 'we hope that you choke' enacts revolt against imposed rules and wisdom, while the android of 'Fitter Happier' ('a pig in a cage on antibiotics') and the wished-for alien of 'Subterranean Homesick Alien' dramatize absurd life under others' dictates. Following The Myth of Sisyphus and The Rebel — 'I revolt, therefore we are' — he shows how the songs' 'I' becomes a collective 'we' ('Karma Police', 'Lucky', 'Dollars and Cents') whose revolt, like Sisyphus's conscious walk back down the mountain, affirms life without ever justifying murder. Merleau-Ponty's philosophy of expression then explains why the songs are political anyway: artists express a still-unspoken 'fever' (it took years before 'Nude' could be said), creating a public and a common world — politics as unveiling rather than governing, down to 'Electioneering'''s admission that the band too campaigns for our vote.

samples.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
samples.relation: Three 'Phase Four' essays. Moseley reads the Joker across Batman #1, The Killing Joke, The Dark Knight, A Death in the Family, and Dark Knight Returns as a 'moral monster' who knowingly does evil - and, following Anscombe and Scanlon's guise-of-the-good analysis, pursues aesthetic 'higher values' in a Camus-like affirmation of the absurd, embracing the irrationality Batman's rational moral order cannot fathom. Levin uses X-gene biology (Beast's explanation in Astonishing X-Men, genotype vs phenotype, M-Day) to strip Magneto's Homo sapiens superior claim of any genetic or phenotypic basis, then argues via the moral community of rational persons (Kant's criterion) that mutants and humans share one moral community, condemning both the Registration Act and mutant separatism. O'Neil's prose piece traces Harvey Dent from Calvinist certainty through the acid that scars him to cosmic doubt - quantum randomness, many worlds, Sartre's condemnation to freedom - until Nietzsche's amor fati lets him embrace duality and let the scarred two-headed coin decide good and evil.

samples.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
samples.title: Mr. Monk Meets Alexander the Great
samples.relation: Wittkower argues that Monk's daily, unwinnable war on dirt and disorder is Camus's happy Sisyphus made concrete: Monk vacuums ceilings, touches lampposts, and solves murders knowing the dirt and the murderers will always return ('There's never hope... Hope. I hate hope's guts' in 'Mr. Monk Can't See a Thing'), yet he still finds enough satisfaction to take up the wipe again. Reading Ecclesiastes' vanity alongside the uncaring wasp of the opening, the chapter claims Monk shows us how to live wisely without resignation in an absurd world that does not care. He is paired with Diogenes the Cynic, whose barrel, raw onions, and midday lantern mirror Monk's pot-pie-Tuesdays and his refusal to overlook what everyone else ignores; like Diogenes telling Alexander the Great 'get out of my sun,' Monk lives by his own ideals no matter how society judges him. The essay closes that, like Camus addressing the Dominican monks, we should refuse to 'be reasonable' about evil and disorder and keep struggling without hope, wipe in hand.

samples.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
samples.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
samples.relation: Moosa uses the apocalypse as a moral laboratory: since 'murder' is by definition wrongful killing, Carl's shooting of Shane must be judged by his reasoning (saving his father), and Hobbes's state of nature — 'solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short' — fits Kirkman's world, yet the survivors import morality into it, as when parents mercy-kill their children just as one would turn up a dying child's morphine. Taking up Camus's claim that suicide is the one truly serious philosophical problem, he argues our world is nearly as bad as the zombie landscape, so consistency commits comfortable readers to the same duty of aid (helping sufferers rather than opting out) that justifies the survivors' fighting on. Finally he argues procreation is the worst thing survivors can do — nonexistent children cannot suffer, so Lori's pregnancy and Glenn and Maggie's crib plans are immoral, and adopting existing children as Andrea and Dale did is the consistent course, an obligation that transfers to our world right now.

samples.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
samples.title: Sweet Miracles of (Secular) Faith, Hope, and Love
samples.relation: Florek reconstructs Peart's ethics as Aristotelian virtue ethics: aiming at eudaimonia rather than feeling good, 'Freewill' chooses autonomy and responsibility as virtues, and 'Vital Signs' adds persistence and courage ('courageous convictions will drag the dream into existence'), with a compassionate expansion toward ordinary sufferers in 'Distant Early Warning', 'Red Sector A' ('I must help my mother stand up straight'), and 'Everyday Glory'. Peart's existential consciousness then confronts finitude ('Time Stand Still', the fading memory of 'Vapor Trail'), contingency ('Roll the Bones' — 'Why does it happen? Because it happens'), and the absurd of Sartre and Camus ('The Stars Look Down' — an indifferent universe that answers nothing). The 1997-98 tragedies turn this existential consciousness tragic, and the post-tragic resolution of Vapor Trails and 'Faithless' is a secular faith in hope and love — Peart's answer to 1 Corinthians 13 without God — grounded in being loved by Carrie Nuttall.

samples.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
samples.title: Conquering the Inner Demon
samples.relation: James Lawler casts Buffy as a contemporary allegory of Plato's cave-escaped philosopher and reads the show through Kant: the Slayer moves between a hellish lower world of instrumental appetite and an intelligible higher world of the soul, and Kant's Copernican revolution ('objects must conform to our knowledge') explains Marcie's invisibility in 'Out of Mind, Out of Sight' and the fear-made-flesh Master of 'Nightmares.' Kant's formula that every rational being exists as an end in himself grounds Buffy's duty in 'Anne' ('I am Buffy, the Vampire Slayer'), her rejection of Spike's chip as no substitute for a soul in 'Crush,' and her 'As You Were' admission that using Spike treats him as a mere means. Season Six explores 'too much heaven': Buffy's blissful death in 'The Gift' makes earthly life hell, and only conquering the inner demon — Willow's fear-driven dark magic defeated by Xander's yellow-crayon love in 'Grave' — restores the balance between heavens and hells.

samples.book: 089 - Steve Jobs and Philosophy - For Those Who Think Different
samples.title: Steve Jobs and Philosophy
samples.relation: Knepp asks why Jobs's 'simplicity is the ultimate sophistication' produced the friendly, MoMA-collected Macintosh (the face-like design, the inviting handle, the signed internals) but collapsed into the $6,500 NeXT Cube, answering with Žižek's reading of Hegel in Less than Nothing: the original idea is already self-contradictory, the failure of NeXT (the over-engineered perfect cube, the $100,000 Rand logo trying too hard to be friendly) is its symptom, and the iMac is the second attempt that only the failed first choice makes possible. He grounds this in Kant's Critique of Pure Reason—the antinomies and the phenomenon/noumenon distinction that Hegel radicalized into a world driven by oppositions—finding the dialectic everywhere in Jobs: two sets of parents, orchards and Silicon Valley, 'Apple' as both high-tech and organic, and a childish lowercase signature made with grand cursive flair.

samples.book: 018 - Harley-Davidson and Philosophy - Full-Throttle Aristotle
samples.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
samples.relation: Harman argues the real heroes of Easy Rider are the two Harley-Davidsons: the exploding Captain America bike that drowns out its rider's corpse, the cocaine hidden in the gas tank like a prosthetic organ, and the obscured helmets and muffled dialogue reduce Fonda, Hopper, and Nicholson to 'stowaways and parasites' of their machines. He uses this reversal to attack Kant's Copernican Revolution, on which we could know only how Harleys appear to us and never the things in themselves, and to champion the Whitehead-Deleuze-Latour current in which genes, pickup trucks, bridges, and Harleys are autonomous actors no less than humans, against Plato's two-world heir of appearances and unknowable things. Billy and Captain America's 1960s transgression, he concludes, quietly ends in submission to the power, rhythm, and demands of their bikes.

samples.book: 036 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - I Link Therefore I Am
samples.title: A Link to the Present
samples.relation: Compagno argues that the word 'I' in Zelda simultaneously names Link, the virtual body, and the player, the invisible will, and builds this into a 'Schopenhauerian Console': as Schopenhauer held, we have freedom of action but not freedom of will, since the decisions of the unknowable will never appear in consciousness (against Descartes' free mind and Dennett's Cartesian theater critique). Kant's transcendental subject, standing at the border of experience, becomes the player's perspective from which Hyrule exists, what Foucault would call an empirical-transcendental doublet. The payoff: Link's quest is fated and scripted, yet the player wills it in a perpetual present, enacting Schopenhauer's lesson that a determined life is still lived as one's own free act.

samples.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
samples.title: A Link to the Present
samples.relation: Dario Compagno uses Schopenhauer's distinction between freedom of action and freedom of will — consciousness never witnesses the moment of decision, only hears the will's outcomes — to model the player-Link relation in Zelda. He proposes a 'Schopenhauerian Console' against Dennett's Cartesian theater: Link is the immanent virtual body in Hyrule, the player's will is the transcendent force outside it, and Kant's transcendental subject is the perspective on the border of experience that connects the two when the gamer becomes 'Link's player'. Foucault's 'empirical-transcendental doublet' explains why 'I am Link' is ambiguous exactly the way 'I' is ambiguous in real life, pointing at once to a body and to an invisible ruling will.

samples.book: 137 - Alice in Wonderland and Philosophy - Curiouser and Curiouser
samples.title: Deleuze Jam Today
samples.relation: Walks Alice through four theories of time: Augustine's three presents in Confessions (Alice 'was a different person then'; the past exists only as present memory), Kant's time as a subjective form of intuition presupposed by experience (the White Rabbit's anxiety about being late already requires it), Bergson's indivisible duration against spatialized clock time (running fastest with the Red Queen yet ending under the same tree; the Hatter stuck at six o'clock; Zeno's Achilles resolved by indivisible acts), and Deleuze's chronos and aion from The Logic of Sense. Mark W. Westmoreland reads 'jam to-morrow and jam yesterday—but never jam to-day' as pure aion: the present never arrives, only an endlessly subdividing past-future.

samples.book: 072 - Jeopardy! and Philosophy - What Is Knowledge in the Form of a Question
samples.title: Jeopardy! and Philosophy
samples.relation: Ellen Sorg separates knowledge from intelligence using Kant's Critique of Pure Reason: Jeopardy! winners like Ken Jennings exercise only the first knowing power, sensibility - recall of facts as they appear to us - never ascending to the intellect of the Transcendental Analytic or acting on what they know, so Jennings would likely wash out on Survivor. Pragmatism supplies the missing criterion: Peirce and James hold that thought gains its value from its practical consequences and from the modification of conduct, which is what Survivor's fire-building, shelter-making, and Kim Spradlin's 2012-winning social game actually test. Hence Jeopardy! proves its champions knowledgeable, but only Survivor proves anyone intelligent.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 83. Disco Elysium as Philosophy Solipsism, Existentialism, and Simulacra
samples.relation: Khamis reads Disco Elysium's 'Pale'—a property-less substance said to be decaying human thought that consumes reality—through three idealisms. The phasmid's warning that the world might vanish if humans stop thinking it evokes Berkeley's subjective idealism (esse est percipi) but without God as guarantor, leaving Harry in existential dread. The Pale as human-produced 'second nature' laid over 'first nature' evokes Kant's and Schelling's transcendental idealism, while the Pale as decaying signs without signification—like the vacuous dockworker 'sheriffs'—matches Baudrillard's hyperreality and simulacra, where information proliferates as meaning collapses, paralleling the amnesiac Harry's own loss and remaking of self.

samples.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
samples.title: The Wire and Philosophy
samples.relation: Zizek reads The Wire as subject-realism, a city's collective self-staging (with Simon as its DJ-curator) of the class struggle between the two Americas, where postmodern institutions play the Olympian gods and the self-propelling abstraction of capital is the Lacanian Real running the show, a point he anchors in Marx's prosopopoeia of commodities and 'real abstraction'. Following Jameson he catalogues the show's utopian gestures woven into reality (Frank's dream of revitalizing the port, Colvin's Hamsterdam, Prezbo's dice-based math, Avon and Stringer's last drink, D'Angelo's family utopia), then argues the Major Crimes unit of McNulty, Freamon, Kima, and Omar is a proto-Communist conspiratorial collective whose honest individual resistance (from Snot Boogie to McNulty's firing) merely feeds the system's self-reproduction. Hence his provocation: the only radical step beyond Simon's social-democratic reformism is the strike of the 'inherent transgressors', withdrawing the resistance that keeps the system alive so that Fate itself, not just its victims, can be changed.

samples.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
samples.title: The Possibility of a Non-Repressive Civilization
samples.relation: Simon Clark reads Romero's four Dead films through Freud's repressive hypothesis: the zombie is the return of the repressed, an embodiment of Eros and Thanatos whose bite is at once erotic and regressive (the devouring mouth read as the vagina dentata, via Barbara Creed), and it advances exactly as civilization's authority breaks down — Mr. Cooper's failed patriarchy in Night of the Living Dead, the mall turned domain of lawless pleasure in Dawn of the Dead. Against Freud's conclusion that repression is necessary, Marcuse's Eros and Civilization supplies the hope of a non-repressive order in which liberated instinct turns toil into play, which Clark finds realized in Day of the Dead's beach ending, where Sarah, John, and McDermott survive pleasurably in the absence of zombies. Land of the Dead goes further: the zombies under Big Daddy evolve, use tools, and march on Kaufman's skyscraper, so the Undead martyr becomes the pioneer of Marcuse's gratified civilization — though Sarah's closing nightmare keeps Freud's suspicion alive that every order remains repressive.

samples.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
samples.title: Caring Dogs Watching Flying Pigs
samples.relation: Croskery reads Animals as a beast fable in the tradition of Orwell's Animal Farm that opens with a thought experiment ('If you didn't care what happened to me / And I didn't care for you') and portrays a world without empathy across three corruptible institutions. 'Dogs' dramatizes a malfunctioning marketplace where Adam Smith's invisible-hand justification fails, since success requires lying to those you must trust and ends with the sad old man 'dragged down by the stone'; 'Pigs (3 Different Ones)' targets state corruption from Mary Whitehouse's censorship crusade to war-waging and regulatory capture; and 'Sheep' depicts Marxist false consciousness, the pastoral illusion hiding the slaughterhouse, capped by the Twenty-Third Psalm parody that 'converteth me to lamb cutlets.' The chapter concludes that libertarian, statist, and traditionalist errors each idolize one institution, and that Waters's closing 'Pigs on the Wing' points to the delicate balance of market, state, and community that political philosophy must strike.

samples.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
samples.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
samples.relation: Brian McDonald opposes two arts in Panem: Peeta's Aristotelian mimesis, which delights and instructs (his camouflage station skill and the 'right shade for sunlight on white fur' speech that eases the dying morphling's last moments), and the Capitol's 'perverse imitation' of tragedy in the arena and Caesar Flickerman's interviews, where the audience feels catharsis's pity and fear with none of its insight because they are complicit in inflicting the tragedy. Drawing on Phillip Rieff's notion of 'de-creation,' he links the Remake Center's freakish body modifications to the arena's cruelties as one abandonment of aesthetic and ethical limits, and uses Augustine's 'deceptive sense of omnipotence' from the Confessions plus Ernest Becker's causa-sui project to explain the Capitol's flight from any fixed identity ('You almost look like a real person'). The chapter closes with Katniss's recognition scene in Mockingjay: choosing the artist Peeta over the hunter Gale is how she survives having become a monster herself.

samples.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
samples.title: 11. Beautiful Colors and Unjust Societies
samples.relation: Devon Brickhouse-Bryson asks whether the Society, plainly dystopian with respect to justice, might nonetheless be utopian with respect to beauty. Treating a society as an abstract object—a system of persons ordered into a community, not reducible to its members or its gravBoots and razors—and beauty as harmoniousness, the ordering of parts into a unified whole in the tradition of Aristotle, Aquinas, and Hutcheson, he shows the Color system straightforwardly instantiates that definition, each caste an organ of one well-functioning clock. But the harmony holds only if the castes are genuinely teleologically distinct; if that is mere Gold propaganda, the Society is not beautiful but a cacophony. Either way the chapter's real lesson stands against Plato: identifying justice with each part fulfilling its role conflates beauty with justice, and the Society shows how radically the two can come apart—possibly beautiful and radically unjust at once.

samples.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
samples.title: Chapter 28 - “Autofac”
samples.relation: Dan Dinello reads 'Autofac' as a dystopian counter to cybernetic utopianism: after nuclear war, self-perpetuating automatic factories with robotic trucks, cameras and humanoid robots keep overproducing useless goods and consuming scarce resources, immutably executing their programming while humans who plead 'we can run our own lives' are condemned to redundancy. Tracing cybernetics from Norbert Wiener's anti-aircraft feedback systems through B.F. Skinner's Walden Two, it argues Dick dramatizes the totalitarian implications of treating humans as machines to be controlled 'for their own good', and the dehumanizing logic of a late capitalism whose profits depend on reckless overproduction, where the system 'gets top priority' and 'mere people come second'. The ending - the factories seeding microscopic self-replicating machinery - completes the vision of a technocratic system expanding and replicating to the possible extinction of humanity.

samples.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: John Irish reads the Amazon series' Vault 33 as Locke's Two Treatises staged and then betrayed: Overseer elections (Betty Pearson against Reg McPhee and Woody Thomas), town-council deliberation over captured Vault 32 raiders, and Lucy's 1950s-styled domesticity all mimic natural equality, consent of the governed, majority rule, and the preservation of property. Norm's discovery that every election is rigged in favor of cryo-preserved technocrats from Vault 31, that Lucy's marriage 'application' is engineered population control, and that Vault-Tec executives - including Lucy's mother Barb - voted to launch the Great War itself shows Locke's forms of consent, law, and rights preserved as empty ceremony. The chapter's argument is that Enlightenment liberalism stripped of transparency becomes authoritarian experiment management: consent becomes choreography in a commonwealth that is really a lab, right down to composting the raiders' bodies.

samples.book: 123 - The Handmaid's Tale and Philosophy - A Womb of One's Own
samples.title: 2. Dystopia from a Woman’s Point of View
samples.relation: Robison-Greene reads The Handmaid's Tale as Atwood's answer to Nineteen Eighty-Four—a dystopia 'from the female point of view'—comparing how both regimes suppress critical thought by banning women's reading, rewriting texts (the Marx slogan 'from each according to her ability' passed off as St. Paul), and manufacturing perpetual war. She deploys Nietzsche's 'monumental' abuse of history, Kierkegaard's leap of faith (Offred's three contradictory versions of Luke's fate), and doublethink to show that believing contradictions becomes both the regime's tool and the victim's survival strategy. The woman's lens adds that reducing women to reproductive function (Marthas, Aunts, Jezebels) thrives where thinking is suppressed, that Beauvoir's point about women's complicity in their oppression is embodied by the Aunts, and that Offred and Nick's affair, like Winston and Julia's, is the act of freedom the Party can never quite own.

samples.book: 025 - The Beatles and Philosophy - Nothing You Can Think that Can't Be Thunk
samples.title: CHAPTER 1 “LET’S GET REAL, REAL GONE FOR A CHANGE”
samples.relation: The chapter argues that Elvis's Sun recordings — the staged rupture in 'Milkcow Blues Boogie' ('That don't move me. Let's get real, real gone for a change') and the accidental 'acting the fool' emergence of 'That's All Right' — enacted an epistemological revolution: a leap out of modernity's rationalized, disembodied mode into repressed bodily affect, defining American cool as affective authenticity against Bill Haley's affected performativity. Elvis's immersion in a Black Memphis neighborhood and his emulation of Black performers made him a catalyst for racial-musical integration and the 'visceral empathy' that prepared desegregation, while the panic of critics (Sinatra, the Times, Congressman Celler) is reread via Hegel's 'tarrying with the negative' as the resistance Geist needs for its self-overcoming. Creative novelty is described with Whitehead's and William James's metaphors — the 'lure of feeling,' sudden phase transition, radical empiricism in what Elvis kept or dropped onstage — with his 'did it make me feel good' studio criterion and a Zen-like mushin statesmanship of loosing egoic control in the band.

samples.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
samples.title: The Awakened One
samples.relation: Callis reads Holmes as a Buddhist practitioner despite the cocaine and the cigars in the coalscuttle: 'You see, but you do not observe' and 'The emotional qualities are antagonistic to clear reasoning' match Vipassana bare attention and the Theravada ideal of the cool, rational, emotionally distant sage, and his improvised violin scraping works like Thich Nhat Hanh's walking meditation — a witness without commentary. The picture is completed by Doyle's Buddhism of Ceylon in The Sign of Four, Holmes's two years 'spending some days with the head lama' in Tibet ('The Empty House'), and his sitting 'like some strange Buddha' in 'The Veiled Lodger.' She maps his method onto the Yoga Sutras' dharana, dhyana, and samadhi — patient attention to the blood-scratched plaster, sustained fixation on the crime scene, ego-surrendering contemplation — making Holmes an 'awakened one' who loves truth for its own sake while Watson lives on autopilot.

samples.book: 018 - Harley-Davidson and Philosophy - Full-Throttle Aristotle
samples.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
samples.relation: Priest argues that Pirsig's Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance is far more genuinely Zen than its disclaimer admits: once riding becomes effortless, the dissolution of the subject-object distinction that Dogen calls genjokoan arrives on the open road ('you ARE the driving and the road and the elements'), and the Harley's relaxed posture and low-revving thug-thug-thug rhythm make it a better vehicle for suchness than cars or whinier bikes. Even maintenance done as an end in itself is genjokoan, and because ultimate reality erases every conceptual distinction, care of self, others, and the bike amount to the same thing, the Mahayana ground of compassion; the mountain-and-water Zen saying resolves the paradox that the unconceptualized and the conceptualized are one. Suffering, on the Buddhist diagnosis Priest applies, comes from imposing conceptual grids that see the world wrong, and seeing it aright dissolves it.

samples.book: 164 - The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy - Everything Is Fire
samples.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy
samples.relation: A cultural history of the coffeehouse frames Larsson's caffeine-soaked cast: the 'penny universities' where Addison brought philosophy out of closets to coffee-house tables, Diderot and Marx plotting at the Café de la Régence, Trotsky at the Café Central, and the Viennese 'meridians of loneliness' that fit Salander's i am an alien T-shirt, Blomkvist hearing his sentence at Kafé Anna, and Niederman's need to sit among people he despises. Ritzer's McDonaldization and 'Starbuckization' explain the characters' Billy's Pan Pizza and chain-café habits as rationalization's homogenizing disenchantment, against which Henrik Vanger's slowly sipped Norrland coffee stands for an older ethics of conversation and community. The chapter closes with the counter-image Larsson's addicts never reach: the Zen tea ceremony of Suzuki and Kakuzo, tranquility emanating from inner consciousness and 'the cup of humanity.'

samples.book: 005 - The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy - One Book to Rule Them All
samples.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
samples.relation: Jennifer McMahon and Steve Csaki compare Tolkien with Zen Buddhism and Taoism on four themes while insisting on the real differences. Tolkien's talking trees (Old Man Willow, Treebeard's 'half awake' forest) invite comparison with Buddhist universal sentience and Dogen's walking mountains, but Tolkien anthropomorphizes where Buddhism grants non-human modes of sentience; the hobbits' ties to the Shire echo dependent origination, though Tolkien's stewardship and preference for the domesticated Shire over sinister wild nature remain Western. Frodo's succession of mentors (Bilbo, Gandalf, Aragorn, and the unlikely 'Master Samwise') parallels the Zen master-student relation, while Tolkien's war of light against darkness - nine Walkers against nine Riders - is decisively not the Taoist balance of yin and yang, for Taoists destroying either cosmic force would itself produce evil.

samples.book: 006 - Baseball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Batter's Box
samples.title: What’s Wrong with Generalization
samples.relation: Brannigan uses Japanese baseball to ask what is wrong with cultural generalization. He presents the Bushido case — samurai-style self-denial, absolute loyalty (Kawakami's Yomiuri Giants), Suisha Tobita's 'training of death,' resolve (konjo), team harmony (wa), and a relational self grounded in Buddhism's no-self and Confucian identity-through-relationships — then tests it against counter-evidence: Sadaharu Oh's flamingo swing owed as much to individual talent and Hiroshi Arakawa's unconventional kendo-and-aikido coaching as to sensei imitation, the 'new breed' (Ochiai, Egawa) flouts the old ways, and William Kelly's 'Whiting problem' warns against polarizing Japanese and American baseball. The chapter's 'three strikes' against the label 'Japanese baseball' conclude that generalizations become dangerous when treated as monolithic nets cast over an entire culture.

samples.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
samples.title: Hakuna Matata, Bodhisattva
samples.relation: Sets up Disney's maxim 'Hey kid, you can be a hero' as the direct opposite of Zen's 'Hey kid, you can be a buddha': escapism versus liberation, told through the life of Dogen, whose monastic choice parallels Disney hero narratives. Mickey in Steamboat Willie — a bundle of still frames with no sound and no real 'he' — illustrates the Buddha's three marks of existence (emptiness, impermanence, frustration), and the chapter argues Disney products are calibrated distractions from these marks while Dogen counsels facing them, with Ariel's Andersen fate as the price of fantasy. It closes on Disney's merchandising machine (Yoda, Star Wars sequels, direct-to-video cash grabs) as everything the countercultural minimalist Yoda or Baloo's bare necessities stand against, concluding that real hakuna matata is accepting impermanence rather than escaping it.

samples.book: 107 - Deadpool and Philosophy - My Common Sense Is Tingling
samples.title: 28. Zen and the Art of Deadpool
samples.relation: The chapter argues Deadpool's unconventional style belies a Zen Buddhist disposition: created as a balance of Spider-Man's wit and Wolverine's lethality (against his disciplined template Deathstroke), he displays mushin, the no-mind calm of the trained martial artist under fire. His story is mapped onto the Four Noble Truths - dukkha in the suicidal depression over his incurable cancer scarring, samudaya in his attachment to belonging that he masks with jokes and loner behavior, nirodha in his ended relationships with Death and Siryn, and magga in shooting himself in the head at the end of Dark Reign as a perverse stilling of the mind. His fourth-wall awareness is read as piercing maya, the veil of illusion, an enlightenment no other Marvel character shares, though he remains 'not a good Buddhist' since he still wallows in ego and attachment.
